[quote=sikirsk;59643954][b]Investigation II[/b] (Better version)

[i]Sikirsk has recently found remnants of the crash, today this part was lifted out by the [b]Sikirskian Company "Sibir - Civil-Naval Corporation"[/b]. They pulled out of the water: [b]The cockpit.[/b] This included logs from the Pilot and the First Officer, and a Black Box T-T consisting of vocal logs from the pilots. Oceanice claimed to help, but has now been banned from Sikirskian territory in all ways, mostly because of classified reasons.
[/i]
[i]Besides the logs, small parts of the engines have been discovered. With one of latest found parts having confirmed human interaction. Besides the engine being 60% being completly obliterated, Engineers still have confirmed that someone had broken several parts, which would lead to the engine most likely overheating and catching fire mid-flight, which aligns with the logs and the restructured and visualised scene.[/i]

The logs show that the First Officer went to the back of the airplane for a bathroom break, during this, the rear-mounted left engine bursted into flames and the pilot tried to struggle the airplane into stability, this succeeded until automatic fire suppression systems failed, and the fire spread to the right engine, which caused the airplane to lose propulsion. The airplane was already in descent at this moment, heading towards northern Hydronia. In the earlier panic the pilot changed course without knowing. In their struggle the pilot claimed to not being able to make it to any airport. So he decided to head for a (not-so-soft) water landing. The airplane reached low altitude when the fire, which was still active, broke of one of the main flaps, according to the now returned First Officer, crippling the pilot's ability to make a slow descent towards the water. 

In the final stages of the audio logs, the pilot mentioned that he couldnt pull up anymore, and tried to land whatever the cost. A loud 'clank' was heard and the recording went silent, with screams just before that. Many theories arose by those who viewed the recording, one of the most popular theories arose after the pulling up of the cockpit, that the back of the airplane hit the water, (as hard as concrete) first, which caused the rest of the airplane to instantly clamp down onto the water, causing the cockpit, including the frontal airplane, being broken off. Resting on a large underwater peak, making it one of the first detectable airplane parts.
